According to research published in BMC Immunology, circulating T-cell receptor repertoires demonstrate distinct diversity, overlap, and segment usage patterns across these clinical cohorts. T cells play a vital role during hepatitis B virus infection by mediating both protective immunity and immunopathology. In-depth profiling of the complementarity-determining region 3 within the T-cell receptor provides critical insights into the composition and functional capacity of circulating T-cell populations. Prior to this investigation, the specific repertoire characteristics of the T-cell receptor alpha-chain and beta-chain across individuals with varying hepatitis B infection and vaccination statuses remained incompletely understood. To systematically evaluate these immune features, researchers employed high-throughput sequencing to profile the alpha-chain and beta-chain complementarity-determining region 3 repertoires within peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The study cohort comprised six inoculation-positive responders to hepatitis B vaccination, six individuals diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B, and five healthy donors. The research team systematically compared the frequency, diversity, sequence similarity, and variable and joining segment usage across the three examined groups. Sequence diversity comparisons demonstrated that the chronic hepatitis B group harbored significantly fewer unique alpha-chain and beta-chain complementarity-determining region 3 sequences than both the inoculation-positive responder group and the healthy donor group. Repertoire overlap analysis revealed marked differences in segment utilization among the study cohorts. The BUB overlap index for alpha-chain variable segments was significantly higher in inoculation-positive responders than in individuals with chronic hepatitis B (P = 0.0073) and healthy donors (P = 0.0317). For beta-chain variable segments, a significantly higher BUB index emerged specifically between inoculation-positive responders and chronic hepatitis B patients (P = 0.0002). Furthermore, identical alpha-chain complementarity-determining region 3 sequences were preferentially shared among individuals within each respective group, whereas beta-chain joining segment usage remained relatively stable across all three cohorts. The investigators concluded that circulating T cells display distinct alpha-beta complementarity-determining region 3 repertoire profiles in inoculation-positive responders and chronic hepatitis B patients. These observed signatures delineate immune differences linked to hepatitis B vaccination responsiveness and chronic disease state, which may help enhance understanding of protective vaccine-induced immunity and inform future investigations into alpha- and beta-chain strategies for hepatitis B virus diagnosis and prevention. The study, published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, examined how pegylated interferon-alpha (PEG-IFNα) and PD-1 blockade alter the circulating inflammatory proteome in patients whose viral replication is already suppressed by nucleos(t)ide analogues. By profiling plasma samples over a 24-week period, the team found that while both therapies induce immune remodeling, the breadth and timing of these changes differ significantly between the two treatment modalities. The investigation focused on 25 patients with chronic hepatitis B who were receiving either PD-1 blockade or PEG-IFNα therapy. The cohort was divided into two groups: ten patients received PD-1 blockade, and fifteen patients received PEG-IFNα. All participants were nucleos(t)ide analogue-suppressed. Plasma samples were collected at three distinct time points: baseline, week 12, and week 24, providing a longitudinal view of how the proteome evolved in response to each therapy. The researchers performed longitudinal plasma proteomic profiling using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Of the proteins measured, seventy-seven passed the quality-control criteria and were included in the final analysis. The study employed linear mixed-effects models to analyze longitudinal protein changes. The primary results indicated that PEG-IFNα induced substantially broader longitudinal proteomic remodeling compared to PD-1 blockade. Most of the significant protein changes in the PEG-IFNα group occurred within the first 12 weeks of treatment. In contrast, the PD-1 blockade group showed a more limited range of proteomic shifts. Treatment-by-time analyses revealed distinct trajectories for the two therapies, highlighting differential changes in several key inflammatory markers, including IL-18R1, TNF, CX3CL1, CXCL9, and CXCL10. The researchers also evaluated the association between these proteomic changes and clinical response, defined as a decline in hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) of at least one log10 IU/mL by week 24. Using responder–non-responder comparisons and Spearman’s rank correlation, the team identified treatment-specific patterns linked to this favorable decline. In the PD-1 blockade cohort, IL-10 emerged as the leading exploratory signal associated with HBsAg decline. In the PEG-IFNα cohort, IL-12B, CDCP1, and FGF-21 were more prominent in the response-associated analyses. However, the study emphasizes that these response-related associations did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction. Consequently, the authors classified these findings as exploratory rather than definitive biomarkers. The findings support the potential value of longitudinal proteomics for mechanistic and biomarker studies of HBV functional-cure strategies. By demonstrating that favorable HBsAg decline is accompanied by treatment-specific rather than universal proteomic signatures, the research highlights the potential value of tracking dynamic immune changes over time. Limitations of the study include the relatively small sample size, with only ten patients in the PD-1 blockade group and fifteen in the PEG-IFNα group. Virion Therapeutics Reports Progress Towards HBV Functional Cure with Continued HBsAg Declines in All Patients and No Viral Rebound Two Plus Years Following a VRON-0200 Prime Dose, at AASLD’s The Liver Meeting® 2026 Business Wire Mon, November 9, 2026 at 11:30 AM CST 5 min read Highlights from the Data Presentation VRON-0200 was safe and well tolerated, with no serious treatment-related adverse events, treatment discontinuations, or treatment-related clinical laboratory abnormalities reported During long-term follow up (LTFU), up to 2+ years following a VRON-0200 prime dose: No patients (0%; 0/26) experienced HBsAg rebound, with durable and deepening HBsAg declines observed in all patients (100%; 26/26) HBsAg mean annualized declines were 5.6-fold greater than historical rates observed in patients receiving NUC-only therapy 14 (54%) and 6 (23%) patients had a >0.5 log10 IU/mL and >1.7 log10 IU/mL decline from Day 1, respectively, with 8 patients (31%) having HBsAg levels <10 IU/mL (3 with HBsAg loss) A single VRON-0200 dose combines ease of administration, a favorable safety profile, and durable anti-HBV activity, supporting its potential as an interferon-sparing immune modulator for HBV Functional Cure strategies, alone, or in combination treatments PHILADELPHIA, November 09, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Virion Therapeutics, LLC, a clinical-stage biotechnology company, developing novel T cell-based immunotherapies that utilize checkpoint modifiers, today announced at AASLD's The Liver Meeting®, in Denver, CO, that an intramuscular prime dose of VRON-0200 alone, its novel, first-in-class, immunotherapy for HBV Functional Cure, induced anti-HBV activity with continued HBsAg declines, without rebound, up to 2+ years post dosing, in all chronically HBV-infected treated patients. These data, presented as a late breaking oral presentation, by Dr. Grace Wong, M.D., from the Chinese University of Hong Kong, also highlighted VRON-0200's favorable safety and tolerability profile, and viral biomarker data, through Day 360. Professor Grace Wong, M.D., from the Chinese University of Hong Kong, one of the study investigators, commented: "What stands out from these VRON-0200 data is that no HBsAg rebound was observed in any patient, and we have observed continued declines in HBsAg levels in all patients during long-term follow-up. New antivirals being developed for HBV Functional Cure are changing the treatment landscape and providing new options for our patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. However, to-date, most patients who lose HBsAg during treatment will rebound following treatment discontinuation. Restoring a patient's own immune responses against the virus with immune modulators and/or therapeutic vaccines is now considered an important strategy to help prevent rebound and improve treatment responses. These long-term VRON-0200 follow up data suggest that it has potential as a safe, easy to administer interferon-sparing immune modulator to address this issue." Story Continues "Immune modulators and therapeutic vaccines have an important role in improving HBV Functional Cure responses. "What is remarkable is that not only was there no HBsAg rebound after 2+ years, but the addition of a prime VRON-0200 dose to suppressive antiviral therapy also resulted in a rate of HBsAg decline that was 5.6 times greater than the historical rate observed in patients on antiviral therapy alone," said Dr. Sue Currie, Chief Operating Officer of Virion Therapeutics. "Its safety, ease of use, and durable anti-HBV activity provide the rationale for evaluating VRON-0200 in a broader range of HBV-infected patients; our SPARK-B Phase 2B study will evaluate off-treatment Functional Cure following nucleos(t)ide discontinuation and will include patients with baseline HBsAg levels up to 3,000 IU/mL. We are excited to advance the VRON-0200 program with the goal of improving Functional Cure rates for the almost 260 million people living with chronic HBV worldwide." Professor Ed Gane, M.D., from the University of Auckland, and one of the study investigators, noted: "The development of new HBV treatments that could produce durable loss of HBV DNA and HBsAg after a finite course of treatment has eluded the field for decades. Finally, we are seeing novel therapies, such as bepirovirsen, that will provide finite treatment options for some of our chronically HBV-infected patients. VRON-0200, with its ability to restore broad and durable anti-HBV immune responses, could become the key component of future combination regimens to both improve the rate of functional cure and also increase the size of the eligible patient population, simply through the addition of a single, well tolerated intramuscular injection. I look forward to continuing to follow VRON-0200's progress as it advances into later stage clinical trials." The presentation is available for download at www.VirionTx.com and more details of this study can be found at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT06070051). About Chronic Hepatitis B Despite a preventative vaccine, cases of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) continue to rise, with an estimated 254 million persons infected worldwide and 1.1 million deaths per year from HBV-related liver complications. Chronic HBV remains a global health issue with a high unmet medical need since there is no cure available. The current standard of care requires lifelong antiviral therapy to maintain control of the virus. Current and investigational HBV Functional Cure treatments have been limited by their inability to restore a patient's own immune responses against the virus. As a result, once treatment is discontinued, and the antiviral agents are no longer present, viral rebound typically occurs. As a result, immune modulators are now considered necessary for future cure treatment strategies. About VRON-0200 VRON-0200 is an investigational therapeutic immunotherapy designed with the goal of providing a functional cure for chronic HBV infection. Clinical data from an ongoing Phase 1b trial have shown VRON-0200 to be safe and well tolerated, and, when given as a single intramuscular dose, was immunogenic, and able to "Spark" anti-HBV activity in chronically HBV-infected patients on nucleos(t)ide therapy alone, and, also, when given with combination antiviral therapies. These results suggest the potential of VRON-0200 to be a key backbone immune modulator for HBV functional cure treatments. About Virion Therapeutics (Virion) Virion Therapeutics, LLC is a clinical-stage company developing novel immunotherapies that utilize proprietary checkpoint modifiers to enhance/restore, broaden, and elicit sustained immune responses, with the goal to cure cancer and chronic infectious diseases. Virion's pipeline now includes its lead VRON-0200 clinical program, and several additional IND-enabling programs, such as its VRON-0300 oncology program for advanced solid tumors, leveraging its proprietary platform technologies. In an internal validation cohort, the top-performing CatBoost algorithm distinguished hepatocellular carcinoma from non-cancerous nodules with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.903. Distinguishing hepatocellular carcinoma from non-hepatocellular carcinoma nodules remains challenging in patients diagnosed with hepatitis B virus infection. To address this diagnostic setting, researchers evaluated ten machine learning algorithms using baseline clinical variables, laboratory indicators, and circulating tumor DNA methylation markers to construct an interpretable framework for individualized risk assessment following nodule detection. Discover more Bioengineering consulting services Health health The study cohort included 586 patients, with 217 adjudicated hepatocellular carcinoma outcomes. The researchers retained an existing partition of 411 patients in the training set and 175 patients in the internal validation set. Ten candidate algorithms underwent nested stratified cross-validation with ten outer folds and five inner folds using regularized candidate settings and a one-standard-error selection rule, with model selection and classification thresholds established solely on training data. Discover more Track Biotech Tour Colleges Donate to Research Find Study Aids Feature selection conducted with Boruta and LASSO retained eleven baseline predictors: patient age, presence of cirrhosis, maximum intrahepatic nodule diameter, alpha-fetoprotein, lens culinaris agglutinin-reactive alpha-fetoprotein percentage, and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin. The remaining retained variables included albumin-bilirubin grade, aspartate aminotransferase, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and two circulating tumor DNA methylation markers, HIST1H3G/ACTB and OTX1/ACTB. Among all evaluated algorithms, the frozen CatBoost model achieved the highest diagnostic metrics on the 175-patient internal validation set. In addition to an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.903, the model demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.800, a specificity of 0.818, an overall accuracy of 0.811, a positive predictive value of 0.722, a negative predictive value of 0.874, an F1 score of 0.759, and a Youden index of 0.618. To ensure interpretability, the investigators performed Shapley Additive Explanations analysis on the CatBoost model. This technique quantified and visualized the individual contribution of each clinical parameter, laboratory indicator, and methylation readout toward model predictions, clarifying the influence of specific features on estimated malignancy probabilities. While the integrated CatBoost model showed potential as an auxiliary tool for individualized assessment of cancer likelihood following nodule detection, the authors noted important study limitations. In particular, the reliance on historically derived feature selection and the reuse of the internal validation partition may limit the robustness of the reported validation results. content: 1990—2021年全球乙型肝炎病毒相关疾病年龄别负担特征、驱动因素量化及至2050年的趋势预测 《Tropical Medicine and Health》:Global age-specific burden of HBV-related diseases, 1990–2021, with projections to 2050 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月10日 来源:Tropical Medicine and Health 3.9 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 背景:普及儿童免疫接种已使年轻人群中乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)相关疾病的疾病负担有所下降,但人口老龄化正在增加老年人群的相关疾病负担。本研究评估了1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病的年龄别趋势,量化了驱动因素,并对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测,以期为优化预防策略提供依据。 方法:研究人员利用2021年全球疾病负担研究(Global Burden of Disease 2021,GBD 2021)数据,分析了1990—2021年间HBV相关疾病的发病率、患病率、死亡及伤残调整生命年(disability-adjusted life-years,DALYs)趋势。研究人员按年龄组(<20岁、20—54岁、≥55岁)对分析结果进行分层,采用Das Gupta分解法定量评估疾病负担变化的驱动因素,并按社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)描述地理分布格局。研究人员应用贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)建模对至2050年的疾病负担进行预测。 结果:1990年至2021年,全球HBV相关疾病年龄标化发病率、患病率、死亡率及DALY率均下降,而死亡与DALY的绝对数量增加。年龄分层分析显示,<20岁人群的所有疾病负担指标均急剧、一致下降;20—54岁人群及更显著的是≥55岁人群的降幅较为温和且病例数量增加。分解分析表明,流行病学改善驱动了年轻人群疾病负担的下降,而人口增长与老龄化抵消了老年人群中的这些获益。地理分布上,最高疾病负担仍集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚,而高SDI地区维持在最低水平。相对变化显示全球<20岁人群发病率降幅显著,而老年人群降幅较小。预测提示,尽管总体率将持续下降,≥55岁人群的绝对疾病负担将持续上升至2050年。 结论:尽管HBV相关疾病负担在年轻人群中持续下降,人口增长与老龄化正重塑全球HBV疾病负担格局,使其向≥55岁人群转移,凸显了针对性预防与管理策略的必要性。 一、研究背景与问题提出 欢迎领取《类器官应用方案 3D之旅》 领 取 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)感染仍是全球重大公共卫生挑战,其健康影响远超急性感染,还包括肝硬化和肝细胞癌等严重长期结局。随着预防控制策略推进与人口结构变化,HBV相关疾病流行病学已发生深刻转变:普及儿童免疫接种改变了年轻一代疾病趋势,而快速人口老龄化则形成了截然不同的疾病负担路径。既往研究多聚焦总体时间趋势、区域差异或疾病构成的特定组分,且年龄特异性模式、分解分析与年龄-时期-队列效应等分析视角常被单独考察,未在统一框架内整合评估;既往感染队列老化所致的老年人群绝对疾病负担上升趋势尚不明确。理解HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别转变对未来预防与管理策略制定至关重要。 二、研究开展概况 研究人员基于GBD 2021数据(覆盖204个国家和地区1990—2021年),将年龄别负担评估、基于社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)的区域比较、Das Gupta分解与贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)预测整合于单一分析框架,量化了流行病学变化、人口老龄化与人口增长对疾病负担变化的贡献,并预测年龄别轨迹至2050年。核心结论为:全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别分化日益显著,人口增长与老龄化正推动疾病负担向≥55岁人群转移。 关键方法概括:研究数据源自GBD 2021数据库(204个国家和地区1990—2021年),以整合急性乙型肝炎、慢性乙型肝炎(含乙肝相关肝硬化)和乙肝相关肝癌的HBV总负担为结局指标,采用发病率、患病率、死亡及DALYs计数和年龄标化率评估负担;运用Das Gupta分解法将绝对变化拆分为流行病学率、年龄结构与人口规模三类效应;应用R软件BAPC包构建年龄-时期-队列模型,以1990—2011年数据拟合、2012—2021年数据回溯验证并以平均绝对百分比误差(mean absolute percentage error,MAPE)评估预测性能,同时设定≥55、≥60、≥65岁三种老年界点开展敏感性分析。 三、研究结果 (一)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病年龄别负担:2021年全球HBV相关疾病发病6851万例,年龄标化发病率848.62/10万,较1990年下降41.61%;患病2.9123亿例,标化患病率3583.57/10万,下降39.05%;死亡64.918万例,标化死亡率7.57/10万,下降37.88%;DALYs达2147万,标化率252.48/10万,下降39.36%。年龄分层显示<20岁组所有指标一致下降;20—54岁与≥55岁组绝对负担轻微上升而率仅温和下降。疾病谱方面,急性乙型肝炎集中于<20岁组,HBV相关肝硬化DALY计数在20—54岁组最高,≥55岁组HBV相关肝癌DALY计数增幅最大且DALY率持续最高。 (二)全球HBV相关疾病负担变化的驱动因素:总体人群中流行病学率下降是各负担指标下降的主要贡献者(如发病例数变化中流行病学率贡献369.46%的下降,人口增长抵消270.62%,年龄结构仅贡献1.16%);年龄分层显示流行病学率效应在<20岁组最显著,而20—54岁及≥55岁组中年龄结构与人口规模的贡献常超过流行病学率改善的减少量,≥55岁组死亡中人口老龄化与人口增长分别贡献121.31%和113.59%,大幅抵消流行病学改善134.91%的下降。敏感性分析证实界点为≥55、≥60或≥65岁时结论一致。 (三)2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理分布:最高负担集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚部分地区,最低年龄标化率见于西欧、北美和大洋洲等高SDI地区;<20岁组全球负担低,20—54岁组为发病与患病主要人群,≥55岁组死亡和DALY率显著更高。各年龄组地理分布相似且集中于低、中SDI地区,随年龄增长负担由以发病、患病为主转向以死亡、DALY为主。 (四)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理变化趋势:全球标化发病与患病率普遍下降,发病降幅最大地区为波兰、意大利和中国台湾省,患病降幅最大地区为波兰、沙特阿拉伯和中国台湾省,丹麦、匈牙利和英国降幅最小。年龄分层呈地理异质性:<20岁组几乎所有地区各率值下降超25%,部分地区超75%;20—54岁组俄罗斯联邦和乌克兰死亡与DALY率升幅超100%;≥55岁组英国、俄罗斯联邦及部分欧洲国家死亡和DALY率上升。 (五)按年龄组划分的SDI区域HBV相关疾病负担的相对变化:<20岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均下降,中高SDI区域降幅最大;20—54岁组低SDI区域绝对负担增幅最大、高SDI区域降幅最大;≥55岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均上升,中低SDI区域增长最陡。率值在所有年龄组和SDI区域均下降,<20岁组在中高SDI区域降幅最大,20—54岁和≥55岁组在中或更高SDI区域降幅最大。 (六)2022—2050年全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄组预测:全年龄绝对负担预计持续下降,但年龄别模式差异显著,<20岁和20—54岁组绝对负担下降,≥55岁组上升(如≥55岁组发病例数预计从2030年1250万增至2050年1578万,而<20岁组从722万降至311万)。所有年龄组率值预计下降,<20岁组降幅最大(发病率由2022年394.30/10万降至2050年127.15/10万),≥55岁组降幅最小(703.01降至583.45/10万)。回溯检验显示多数MAPE值低于10%,敏感性分析结果与主分析一致。 四、讨论部分总结 讨论指出,各年龄组间的鲜明分歧是最关键发现,解释了总体率下降与总人群绝对负担上升并存的悖论。<20岁组负担急剧一致下降,流行病学率改善为主导驱动,与疫苗接种在健康婴儿、儿童和青少年中诱导的超过95%血清保护率一致;而老年人疫苗血清保护率降至60%—70%且多出生于普遍接种之前,形成独特流行病学模式。≥55岁组所有绝对指标显著上升(发病增74.10%、患病增87.38%、死亡增42.77%、DALYs增35.86%),人口增长与老龄化联合效应远超流行病学率改善的减少量,人口压力主导了老年人群流行病学格局;这些发现应解释为人群水平模式而非个体纵向转变。地理差异与年龄别异质性并存,部分欧洲区域死亡与DALY率上升超100%,反映预防控制收益分配不均。世界卫生组织(World Health Organization,WHO)2030年消除病毒性肝炎的目标面临疾病负担老龄化的重大人口学挑战。政策启示包括:维持青少年疫苗接种进展(及时接种首针并补种);对≥55岁人群扩大筛查、强化诊断并促进抗病毒治疗;针对不同SDI区域实施差异化策略。局限性包括BAPC模型依赖历史数据、≥55岁组预测不确定性区间(uncertainty intervals,UIs)较宽、未量化疫苗接种与抗病毒治疗贡献及未详察国家内部差异。 五、研究结论部分翻译 总之,尽管全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄标化率(age-standardized rates,ASRs)已下降,≥55岁人群绝对负担却增加,人口增长和老龄化在很大程度上促成了这一转变,抵消了有利流行病学变化带来的减少。区域差异依然显著,低、中SDI地区承担最大负担。预测表明这种年龄相关转变可能持续,凸显实现WHO定义的2030年肝炎消除目标仍面临持续挑战。应对挑战需加强针对性筛查、改善老年人群抗病毒治疗可及性,并实施区域特异性的预防控制策略。 一、研究背景与问题提出乙型肝炎病毒(HBV,hepatitis B virus)感染仍是全球重大公共卫生挑战,其健康影响远超急性感染,还包括肝硬化和肝细胞癌等严重长期结局。随着预防控制策略推进与人口结构变化,HBV相关疾病流行病学已发生深刻转变:普及儿童免疫接种改变了年轻一代疾病趋势,而快速人口老龄化则形成了截然不同的疾病负担路径。既往研究多聚焦总体时间趋势、区域差异或疾病构成的特定组分,且年龄特异性模式、分解分析与年龄-时期-队列效应等分析视角常被单独考察,未在统一框架内整合评估;既往感染队列老化所致的老年人群绝对疾病负担上升趋势尚不明确。理解HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别转变对未来预防与管理策略制定至关重要。二、研究开展概况研究人员基于GBD 2021数据(覆盖204个国家和地区1990—2021年),将年龄别负担评估、基于社会人口学指数(socio-demographic index,SDI)的区域比较、Das Gupta分解与贝叶斯年龄-时期-队列(Bayesian age-period-cohort,BAPC)预测整合于单一分析框架,量化了流行病学变化、人口老龄化与人口增长对疾病负担变化的贡献,并预测年龄别轨迹至2050年。核心结论为:全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄别分化日益显著,人口增长与老龄化正推动疾病负担向≥55岁人群转移。关键方法概括:研究数据源自GBD 2021数据库(204个国家和地区1990—2021年),以整合急性乙型肝炎、慢性乙型肝炎(含乙肝相关肝硬化)和乙肝相关肝癌的HBV总负担为结局指标,采用发病率、患病率、死亡及DALYs计数和年龄标化率评估负担;运用Das Gupta分解法将绝对变化拆分为流行病学率、年龄结构与人口规模三类效应;应用R软件BAPC包构建年龄-时期-队列模型,以1990—2011年数据拟合、2012—2021年数据回溯验证并以平均绝对百分比误差(mean absolute percentage error,MAPE)评估预测性能,同时设定≥55、≥60、≥65岁三种老年界点开展敏感性分析。三、研究结果(一)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病年龄别负担:2021年全球HBV相关疾病发病6851万例,年龄标化发病率848.62/10万,较1990年下降41.61%;患病2.9123亿例,标化患病率3583.57/10万,下降39.05%;死亡64.918万例,标化死亡率7.57/10万,下降37.88%;DALYs达2147万,标化率252.48/10万,下降39.36%。年龄分层显示<20岁组所有指标一致下降;20—54岁与≥55岁组绝对负担轻微上升而率仅温和下降。疾病谱方面,急性乙型肝炎集中于<20岁组,HBV相关肝硬化DALY计数在20—54岁组最高,≥55岁组HBV相关肝癌DALY计数增幅最大且DALY率持续最高。(二)全球HBV相关疾病负担变化的驱动因素:总体人群中流行病学率下降是各负担指标下降的主要贡献者(如发病例数变化中流行病学率贡献369.46%的下降,人口增长抵消270.62%,年龄结构仅贡献1.16%);年龄分层显示流行病学率效应在<20岁组最显著,而20—54岁及≥55岁组中年龄结构与人口规模的贡献常超过流行病学率改善的减少量,≥55岁组死亡中人口老龄化与人口增长分别贡献121.31%和113.59%,大幅抵消流行病学改善134.91%的下降。敏感性分析证实界点为≥55、≥60或≥65岁时结论一致。(三)2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理分布:最高负担集中于撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚部分地区,最低年龄标化率见于西欧、北美和大洋洲等高SDI地区;<20岁组全球负担低,20—54岁组为发病与患病主要人群,≥55岁组死亡和DALY率显著更高。各年龄组地理分布相似且集中于低、中SDI地区,随年龄增长负担由以发病、患病为主转向以死亡、DALY为主。(四)1990—2021年全球HBV相关疾病负担的地理变化趋势:全球标化发病与患病率普遍下降,发病降幅最大地区为波兰、意大利和中国台湾省,患病降幅最大地区为波兰、沙特阿拉伯和中国台湾省,丹麦、匈牙利和英国降幅最小。年龄分层呈地理异质性:<20岁组几乎所有地区各率值下降超25%,部分地区超75%;20—54岁组俄罗斯联邦和乌克兰死亡与DALY率升幅超100%;≥55岁组英国、俄罗斯联邦及部分欧洲国家死亡和DALY率上升。(五)按年龄组划分的SDI区域HBV相关疾病负担的相对变化:<20岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均下降,中高SDI区域降幅最大;20—54岁组低SDI区域绝对负担增幅最大、高SDI区域降幅最大;≥55岁组所有SDI区域绝对负担均上升,中低SDI区域增长最陡。率值在所有年龄组和SDI区域均下降,<20岁组在中高SDI区域降幅最大,20—54岁和≥55岁组在中或更高SDI区域降幅最大。(六)2022—2050年全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄组预测:全年龄绝对负担预计持续下降,但年龄别模式差异显著,<20岁和20—54岁组绝对负担下降,≥55岁组上升(如≥55岁组发病例数预计从2030年1250万增至2050年1578万,而<20岁组从722万降至311万)。所有年龄组率值预计下降,<20岁组降幅最大(发病率由2022年394.30/10万降至2050年127.15/10万),≥55岁组降幅最小(703.01降至583.45/10万)。回溯检验显示多数MAPE值低于10%,敏感性分析结果与主分析一致。四、讨论部分总结讨论指出,各年龄组间的鲜明分歧是最关键发现,解释了总体率下降与总人群绝对负担上升并存的悖论。<20岁组负担急剧一致下降,流行病学率改善为主导驱动,与疫苗接种在健康婴儿、儿童和青少年中诱导的超过95%血清保护率一致;而老年人疫苗血清保护率降至60%—70%且多出生于普遍接种之前,形成独特流行病学模式。≥55岁组所有绝对指标显著上升(发病增74.10%、患病增87.38%、死亡增42.77%、DALYs增35.86%),人口增长与老龄化联合效应远超流行病学率改善的减少量,人口压力主导了老年人群流行病学格局;这些发现应解释为人群水平模式而非个体纵向转变。地理差异与年龄别异质性并存,部分欧洲区域死亡与DALY率上升超100%,反映预防控制收益分配不均。世界卫生组织(World Health Organization,WHO)2030年消除病毒性肝炎的目标面临疾病负担老龄化的重大人口学挑战。政策启示包括:维持青少年疫苗接种进展(及时接种首针并补种);对≥55岁人群扩大筛查、强化诊断并促进抗病毒治疗;针对不同SDI区域实施差异化策略。局限性包括BAPC模型依赖历史数据、≥55岁组预测不确定性区间(uncertainty intervals,UIs)较宽、未量化疫苗接种与抗病毒治疗贡献及未详察国家内部差异。五、研究结论部分翻译总之,尽管全球HBV相关疾病负担的年龄标化率(age-standardized
